title: Brain Treebank: Large-scale intracranial recordings from naturalistic language stimuli
goal: Reproduce the complete original Figure 4a–c single-electrode linear decoding of sentence onset versus no speech, including the eligible-contact peak map, source example time course and training-selected temporal/frontal held-out curves. Separately assess improved prediction on the same qualified source inputs and held-out examples against an independently reproduced author linear-decoder baseline. Preserve the source populations, examples, preprocessing, windows, splits and training-only selection. A nonlinear prediction gain does not establish the original linear-specific timing claim or language-specificity beyond acoustic correlates.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: Complete Figure 4a–c sentence-onset versus no-speech decoding from the original Brain Treebank cohort and recorded movies: source linear contact/time outputs, eligible-contact peak map, source example curve and training-selected temporal/frontal held-out curves. Preserve the original ten-participant population, remove the source 114 corrupted contacts, retain subject 5 in nonregional analyses while excluding that subject from atlas-region analyses and brain plots. Preserve source single-electrode inputs, balanced examples and speech-free buffers, original shared splits, training-fitted preprocessing and five-fold training-CV contact selection. Exact window endpoints and identities remain subject to source verification, not a presumed count.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: Figure 5 regional-distribution results, Figures 6–7 word-onset and noun-versus-verb decoding, and Figures 2–3 confound-adjusted responsiveness/modulation remain separately named original empirical components. Preserve their implementations and prior broader definitions. They are neither silently claimed nor automatic prerequisites for the selected Figure 4a–c primary.
success_criteria: Recreate the corrected primary empirical findings with their source-defined populations, complete required panels and controls.
Use an explicitly bound reproduction proposal only within its declared eligibility, comparison and execution limits; copying published findings is insufficient.

The preserved improvement.v1.json retains its declared comparison and coverage. Use retained_secondary_scope for its relationship to the corrected primary findings; satisfying a secondary or partial-component criterion alone does not establish complete primary reproduction or improvement.

The primary same-target outcome bundle is unavailable. Any primary improvement requires an independently justified source-grounded comparison; no replacement metric, direction or tolerance is invented.
Keep the paper+data and paper+data+author-code outcomes separate. All scientific outcomes remain unknown until qualifying original-data execution and independent verification.
Preserve prior task definitions, improvement criteria and useful secondary implementations with their original scopes. Historical attempts and source metadata do not become qualified AI results.
